stories.name: Jury convicts man of starting the fire that became the Palisades Fire
facts: On Friday, Nov. 20, a federal jury in Los Angeles convicted Jonathan Rinderknecht, 30, on both counts in a retrial: destruction of property by means of fire, and arson (AP, NBC News).
His first trial ended in a mistrial in June after jurors deadlocked 10-2 in favor of acquittal (AP, NBC News).
Prosecutors said he lit a brush fire on Jan. 1, 2025 (the Lachman Fire) that smoldered underground in root systems and flared up again on Jan. 7 as the Palisades Fire (AP, NBC News).
The Palisades Fire killed 12 people; NBC News, citing the LAFD, reported 6,837 structures destroyed and 23,448 acres burned (AP, NBC News).
The defense argued the scene was open to the public for days and suggested fireworks as a cause; prosecutors said camera images showed no fireworks (AP, NBC News).
Rinderknecht showed little apparent reaction to the verdict and hugged his attorneys before leaving (AP).

people.name: Jonathan Rinderknecht
people.verified_action: Stands with his attorneys in federal court as the guilty verdict is delivered; little apparent reaction (AP). Drawn generic and unrecognizable.

stories.visual_notes: Cross-section idea: the courtroom fills the lower part of the frame; its tall back wall opens onto an illustrative night view of the Pacific Palisades hillside above the ocean. A thin glowing line of embers creeps underground through tangled roots from a small Jan. 1 spark on the left to a wall of flame on the ridge at right, an obviously illustrative telling of the prosecution's holdover-fire account. Twelve jurors (six men, six women per NBC) sit in the jury box; a judge at the bench; the generic defendant stands between two attorneys at the defense table. A warm spotlight from above. No faces for the defendant, no text, no victims, no bodies.
stories.confidence: high: the conviction, counts, mistrial history, death toll and the prosecution's holdover theory are reported independently by AP and NBC News. The 12-member jury composition comes from NBC only and is a minor visual detail.
